activation: Only after the coordinator grants the delivery slot following cohorts16/23. No accepted version, catalog/crosswalk/history/count/bank activation, receipt, merge or closure during preparation.

evidence_requirements: Preparation: current guidance favors a single corporate tenant and separate ALZ deployments where multiple tenants are justified; there is no supported ARM predicate for organizational or regulatory need.

Reviewer decision: cite an attributable dated tenant-strategy decision and redacted authoritative inventory reference; document the specific regulatory/business requirements that cannot be met in one tenant and the considered single-tenant alternatives.

Reviewer decision: independently substantiate tenant/ALZ boundaries, workload service/B2B support, collaboration, licensing, audit and JML implications. Neither subscription/resource counts nor Lighthouse registrations prove complete tenant inventory or strategy suitability.
recommendations.limitations: Business and regulatory suitability remain explicit decisions. No tenant names/IDs, directory enumeration, cross-cloud assumption, migration or inferred tenant strategy. EA/MCA can span tenants under their conditions; agreement count is not tenant count.

evidence_requirements: Preparation: reviewed platform automation models distinguish complete isolation from a shared multitenant application with per-tenant service principals; current user-assigned managed-identity federation qualifications apply. No directory/application/pipeline inventory is collected.

Reviewer decision: establish whether multitenant platform automation applies, then cite the approved operating model, isolation rationale and redacted repository/pipeline/identity boundary and privilege-management references.

Reviewer decision: independently demonstrate actual authorized operation, tenant targeting, credential/federation lifecycle, change control, monitoring and recovery. Configuration or a Lighthouse pair does not prove execution, adoption or the owner/authorization rights needed for whole-platform ALZ deployment.
recommendations.limitations: No actual cross-tenant automation, new identity trust/registration/consent, pipeline execution or credentials. Example approaches are not universal workload requirements. Lighthouse's restricted UAA exception does not provide general access administration.

evidence_requirements: Preparation: explicit subscription/RG assignment-to-subscription-definition reference, unique known same-subscription records within the selected boundary and bounded syntactically valid authorization-pair counts only. RG selection does not authorize reading its subscription-level definition.

Reviewer decision: substantiate applicable multitenant management and actual authorized same-identity use with attributable redacted evidence, including intended tasks, supported cloud, selected subscription/RG scopes and least-privilege roles.

Reviewer decision: separately substantiate effective delegated access, current built-in-role/action restrictions, eligible/JIT activation and managing-tenant licensing where applicable. Owner/custom/DataActions roles are unsupported; constrained UAA managed-identity assignments are not general access administration.
recommendations.limitations: Joined registration metadata is partial configuration, not effective authority, identity use, onboarding success, full tenant inventory or directory/billing access. Lighthouse does not delegate tenants/MGs or cross clouds. Public role-reference syntax/counts establish neither supported roles nor permissions. No raw tenant/principal identifiers or private authorization details retained.

evidence_requirements: Preparation: the same strict subscription/RG registration join provides bounded resource-delegation configuration only; it does not identify a partner, CSP reseller, contract or commercial model.

Reviewer decision: explicitly establish whether partner administration applies from an approved redacted agreement/reference, then substantiate customer approval, intended resource scope/tasks, least privilege, removal/audit and current role support.

Reviewer decision: distinguish Lighthouse resource delegation from Entra GDAP/DAP and billing authority; reconcile CSP AOBO and private marketplace-plan restrictions where relevant. No Lighthouse registration can demonstrate whole-tenant administration or partner support effectiveness.
recommendations.limitations: Partner applicability and actual authorized access remain separately attributable decisions. No auto-exclusion from absent registrations, guessed commercial model, new delegation or retained partner-private records.

evidence_requirements: Preparation: CSP guidance identifies the partner as first support contact and requires agreement on case creation and escalation; Lighthouse and GDAP are not evidence of this process.
Reviewer decision: establish CSP applicability explicitly and cite the approved redacted support/request/escalation process, accountable roles, service coverage and agreed response/escalation paths.

Reviewer decision: substantiate communication, current availability and dated exercise or real operation with redacted evidence references, without retaining tickets, personal contact details or confidential partner records.
recommendations.limitations: Manual support-process and operating-effectiveness decision. No support case, message, contact lookup, invented SLA or inferred CSP relationship. Not-applicable requires its own bound rationale.

evidence_requirements: Preparation: pinned ARM shared-view chart/metric enums and explicit subscription/RG view scope must match the unique known resource parent inside the selected boundary. Query bodies, filters, amounts, usage, names and billing identifiers are withheld; private/billing/MG views are not supported projections.

Reviewer decision: establish actual agreement, reporting audience and approved cost-allocation/reporting requirements; demonstrate current appropriate reports/views and their actual use with attributable redacted evidence.

Reviewer decision: substantiate effective RBAC/billing visibility, EA charge policies or CSP Azure Plan/MCA/provider visibility conditions as applicable. Distinguish CSP retail views from partner invoice prices, MCA hierarchy from EA and saved configuration from underlying data, shared access or a pinned dashboard snapshot.
recommendations.limitations: View metadata proves neither reporting outcome, current data, complete costs, invoice access nor financial suitability. MCA MG Cost Management and EA/MCA MG cost-details limitations remain explicit. No query execution, billing-plane reads, prices, usage, permissions or scheduled email.

evidence_requirements: Preparation: EA notification contacts and Bill to invoice contacts have different purposes; MCA billing-account notification guidance differs. There is no subscription-level ARM field proving group-mailbox suitability.

Reviewer decision: establish agreement-specific notification requirements and cite redacted approved configuration/ownership references confirming an appropriate maintained group mailbox and authorized coverage of required categories/cadence.

Reviewer decision: separately substantiate delivery/review/escalation and continuity with dated redacted references; do not retain mailbox addresses, contact identifiers, memberships or message contents. A configured address, action group or budget recipient does not prove billing notification coverage.
recommendations.limitations: Manual group-mailbox suitability and actual notification operation. No mailbox/contact/notification read or change, sent test message, inferred recipient/group or billing access. Upcoming EA WSA-only assignment policy is not proof of notification configuration.

evidence_requirements: Preparation: EA enrollment/departments/accounts/subscriptions, MCA billing account/profiles/invoice sections/subscriptions and CSP partner-managed MPA/customer structures are different. Azure MG/resource hierarchy is not a billing hierarchy.

Reviewer decision: explicitly establish the actual applicable agreement and approved organizational mapping using attributable redacted authoritative references; for EA substantiate department/account mapping and intended billing separation, for MCA the corresponding profile/invoice-section design.

Reviewer decision: demonstrate actual hierarchy, scoped ownership, coverage and current operation, including agreement-specific roles and constraints. Do not retain account/enrollment names/IDs, private contracts, prices or financial records; a subscription belongs to only one EA account or MCA invoice section at a time under applicable rules.
recommendations.limitations: Agreement-specific hierarchy and organizational suitability remain human decisions. No tenant/resource names, counts, MG parents or Lighthouse records infer a contract or prove billing separation. EA quota is not enforcement; billing roles do not imply directory/resource authority. No invented billing-plane ARM resource or scope expansion.
